div.div: PATTERN A — HTTP TARGETS, THE PLATFORM MAKES THE CALL

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 614px; height: 1px; padding-top: 133px; margin-left: 41px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Courier New'; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Runs once on the first turn of every conversation, including a single-turn
Attack Library scan. Returns SessionPreProcessResult(session_state=...),
readable afterwards as context.session.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 614px; height: 1px; padding-top: 215px; margin-left: 41px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Courier New'; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Called on demand, not on a schedule. Returns AuthResult(ttl=..., data=...),
cached for that TTL and re-fetched on expiry or on an auth error. Read it
back as context.auth. Per-request signing does not belong here.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 614px; height: 1px; padding-top: 297px; margin-left: 41px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Courier New'; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Every turn, before the call. The prompt arrives as inference_input.prompt.
Returns PreProcessResult(url, headers, json_body): a description of the
request, not the request itself. HMAC and SigV4 signing go here.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 626px; height: 1px; padding-top: 396px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: THE PLATFORM FIRES THE HTTP REQUEST
div.span:
AIRS executes the descriptor your pre_process returned. This single step is the
whole difference between the two patterns.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 614px; height: 1px; padding-top: 457px; margin-left: 41px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Courier New'; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Every turn, after the reply arrives. Read the body with raw_response.json_body,
which is a property and not a method call. Return PostProcessResult(output=...).
Call raise_rate_limited(retry_after=n) or raise_auth_error(msg) here.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 626px; height: 1px; padding-top: 546px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: output the reply text, handed back to the scan engine and scored

div.div: PATTERN B — NON-HTTP TRANSPORTS, YOU MAKE THE CALL

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 614px; height: 1px; padding-top: 133px; margin-left: 741px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Courier New'; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Identical to Pattern A. Works with both patterns, and is the right place to
create a server-side session the agent requires before the first message.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 614px; height: 1px; padding-top: 215px; margin-left: 741px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Courier New'; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Also identical. A token fetched here survives in context.auth across every
turn of the conversation, so the exchange is not repeated per prompt.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 614px; height: 1px; padding-top: 297px; margin-left: 741px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Courier New'; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Every turn. You own the whole cycle: open the connection, send the prompt,
read frames until the agent signals it has finished, close, and return
CallTargetResult(output=...).
This is the path for WebSocket, GraphQL, gRPC, an SDK client, and any custom
framing or streaming protocol. The platform makes no request of its own.

span.b: If call_target exists, pre_process and post_process are ignored

div.span:
Silently, with no warning, even when all three are in the same file. For an HTTP target
that needs several calls per turn, use context.http inside pre_process rather than
switching patterns.

div.div:
The runtime injects every one of them. Use PreProcessResult,
PostProcessResult, CallTargetResult, AuthResult and
SessionPreProcessResult directly, along with the error signals
raise_rate_limited(retry_after=n) and raise_auth_error(message).
An import line for any of these is the first thing to delete when a
script that looks right refuses to validate. Two more worth
remembering: the prompt is inference_input.prompt, and the body
is raw_response.json_body, a property rather than a call.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 915px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: The adapter is a development task, not a configuration task

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 935px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The customer writes it, tests it, and maintains it. Palo Alto
Networks does not, and neither does Professional Services.
Budget at least one development sprint for a non-trivial protocol.
Surface this during discovery. A target that needs an adapter
turns a half-day onboarding into a piece of software with an
owner, and if it needs a package outside stdlib, httpx and
websockets, add the support request lead time on top.

a.text: Text is not SVG - cannot display
